title: Magnitude 7.7 quake strikes Panama, toppling buildings
title_zh: 巴拿马遭遇7.7级强震，多处建筑倒塌

image.credit: Photo by Çağlar Oskay on Unsplash
image.author: Çağlar Oskay

lead: A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake has struck south-central Panama, damaging buildings and shaking a wide area. About 4.6 million people felt the tremors, though no casualties have yet been reported.
lead_zh: 巴拿马中南部发生7.7级强震，导致建筑物受损，大片地区震感强烈。约460万人感受到震动，目前尚无人员伤亡报告。
preview: The quake struck just before 15:00 local time (18:00 GMT) on Friday, with its epicentre located approximately 6.2 miles (10km) from Pitaloza
preview_zh: 地震发生在当地时间周五15:00前（格林尼治标准时间18:00），震中位于巴拿马中南部皮塔洛萨阿里瓦镇附近约6.2英里（10公里）处。据美国地质调查局称，约460万人感受到中度至强烈震动，并警告影响可能波及广泛。此次地震震源深度仅12公里，浅源地震往往会加剧地表破坏。
paragraphs: The quake struck just before 15:00 local time (18:00 GMT) on Friday, with its epicentre located approximately 6.2 miles (10km) from Pitaloza Arriba in south-central Panama. According to the US Geological Survey, roughly 4.6 million people experienced moderate to severe tremors, and the agency warned that the effects were likely to be widespread. The earthquake occurred at a shallow depth of just 12km, which tends to intensify surface damage.

Footage circulating online appears to show collapsed buildings in Penonomé and Soná, including a man calling out to anyone trapped under rubble. Verified video reveals that one side of Penonomé's cathedral, along with a spire, had crumbled. Another clip showed a local hotel almost completely destroyed. Ricardo Brown, a 74-year-old resident of Herrera province, told Reuters that several homes in his Las Minas neighbourhood had been damaged. "We're scared. The house has cracked and we're afraid it could fall on us," he said.

In Panama City, some 200km from the epicentre, many people evacuated buildings and took to the streets or nearby parks until the shaking subsided. Damage in the capital appears largely confined to debris falling from roofs. President José Raúl Mulino said his entire government was mobilising in response, cautioning that "what happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder." Tsunami warnings were initially issued for 11 neighbouring countries, but the US Tsunami Warning System later confirmed there was no threat.

The Panama Canal, the vital waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific, was unaffected, according to the authority overseeing marine traffic. The earthquake struck just three days before Panama was scheduled to hold a national evacuation drill for a major quake, and it follows devastating earthquakes in Colombia and Venezuela earlier this year. Several large aftershocks near the initial quake could further complicate the situation on the ground.
paragraphs_zh: 地震发生在当地时间周五15:00前（格林尼治标准时间18:00），震中位于巴拿马中南部皮塔洛萨阿里瓦镇附近约6.2英里（10公里）处。据美国地质调查局称，约460万人感受到中度至强烈震动，并警告影响可能波及广泛。此次地震震源深度仅12公里，浅源地震往往会加剧地表破坏。
网上流传的视频似乎显示佩诺诺梅和索纳有建筑物倒塌，其中一段视频中一名男子在瓦砾下呼喊被困者。经核实的画面显示，佩诺诺梅大教堂的一侧及一座尖塔已经坍塌。另一段视频显示当地一家酒店几乎完全损毁。埃雷拉省74岁居民里卡多·布朗告诉路透社，他所在的拉斯米纳斯社区有几处房屋受损。他说：“我们很害怕。这里只有我们两个老人。房子裂了，我们担心它会塌下来。”
在距震中约200公里的巴拿马城，许多人撤离建筑物，涌上街头或坐在附近公园里，直到震动停止。首都的损失似乎主要限于屋顶掉落的碎片。总统何塞·劳尔·穆利诺表示，整个政府正在动员应对，并告诫说“发生的事情不应被用来引发恐慌或混乱”。最初对巴拿马邻国11个国家发布了海啸预警，但美国海啸预警系统随后确认没有威胁。
负责监管巴拿马运河海上交通的机构称，这条连接大西洋和太平洋的重要水道未受地震影响。此次地震发生之际，距巴拿马计划举行全国性大地震疏散演习仅三天，而今年早些时候哥伦比亚和委内瑞拉也遭遇了破坏性地震。主震附近还报告了几次大型余震，可能使当地局势更加复杂。

vocab.note: 地震学术语，英式拼写，美式为 epicenter
用于描述地震能量大小，如 magnitude 7.7
常指地震引起的震动，也可指一般的颤抖
主震后发生的较小地震
不可数名词，常与 collapse 搭配
教堂等建筑顶部的尖顶结构
常与 from 连用，如 evacuate from buildings
英式拼写，美式为 mobilize，指组织资源应对
源自日语，指地震引发的巨浪
如巴拿马运河等通航水路

vocab.zh: 毁灭性的；破坏力极强的

vocab.note: 也可作名词，如 building collapse
此处指震动停止，也可指洪水退去
常用被动语态 be confined to

title_original: Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Panama, damaging buildings
summary_original: Tsunami warnings are issued for neighbouring countries as videos of destruction circulate online.
body_original:
Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Panama, damaging buildings
By
Michael Sheils McNamee
Published
9 October 2026
A massive magnitude 7.7 earthquake has hit Panama, damaging buildings and causing widespread shaking.
About 4.6 million people felt moderate to severe tremors as a result of the quake, according to the US Geological Survey, which has said that the effects of the quake were "likely to be widespread".
It struck just before 15:00 local time (18:00 GMT) on Friday, with an epicentre about 6.2 miles (10km) from the town of Pitaloza Arriba in south-central Panama.
Footage shared online appears to show collapsed buildings in the towns of Penonomé and Soná, including one of a man calling out to anyone trapped under the rubble of a collapsed building. No casualties have so far been reported.
Verified footage shows one side of a cathedral in Penonomé collapsed due to the shaking, as well as one of its spires.
Another video showed a local hotel had almost completely collapsed.
Ricardo Brown, who lives in the southern Herrera province, told news agency Reuters that the earthquake had damaged several homes in his neighbourhood of Las Minas.
"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked and we're afraid it could fall on us," the 74-year-old said.
The full extent of the damage it has caused is not yet clear, though several large aftershocks were also reported near the initial earthquake, potentially complicating the situation on the surface.
The quake was registered as occurring at a depth of just 12km. The shallower the earthquake, the more likely it is to have more severe effects on the surface.
Many people were evacuated from buildings in Panama City, about 200km from the epicentre, and were seen taking to the streets or sitting in nearby parks until the shaking had ceased.
Damage in the capital appears to be limited to that caused by debris falling from roofs.
Panama's President José Raúl Mulino said his entire government was mobilising in response to the earthquake, adding: "What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder."
Tsunami warnings were initially issued for 11 countries neighbouring Panama, before the US Tsunami Warning System confirmed there was no threat.
The Panama Canal - a vital waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans - was unaffected by the earthquake, the authority that oversees marine traffic through it said.
The earthquake comes just three days before Panama was scheduled to hold a national evacuation drill for dealing with a major earthquake.
It also follows devastating earthquakes in Colombia and Venezuela earlier this year.
